# Sizing candidates - grouped comparison (X / Y / Z / M2)

Created 2026-09-26. This is the cross-comparison that four separate studies each
said was "deferred to end-of-session" and nobody ever did. Until now, answering
"which sizing candidate is best" meant opening four JSONs by hand.

**Table generated by** `backtest/tests/exp_sizing_candidate_compare.py`
-> `_sizing_candidate_compare.json`. Do not retype the numbers below; re-run it.

## What these are

All four are **position sizing** candidates: trade a 1.5x larger lot on trades
matching some pre-frozen, entry-causal condition. They do **not** remove trades.

That distinction is the whole reason they are still standing. A removal changes
*which* trades the engine takes, which frees `busy_until` slots and shifts the
cooldown and loss-streak timeline. That cascade measured **3-5x larger than the
direct effect** and killed the Stage B removals 0/4. A sizing arm changes only
the R booked on a trade, never the trade list, so the post-process number is a
real measurement. See the sizing-exemption section of `AGENT_COORDINATION.md`.

## Rollup - the grouped answer

| cand | what it keys on | lanes passed | worst IS | worst OOS | small-n? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M2** | `cur_mag_atr >= 3` (big current magnitude) | **3 / 3** | **+117.1R** | **+18.8R** | no |
| **Z** | regime structure - 4 arms | 6 / 8 | **-71.5R** | +10.8R | no |
| **Y** | 4h EMA-extension pullback - 4 arms | 2 / 12 | **-72.5R** | **-36.8R** | no |
| **X** | HTF 1h break quality - 3 arms | 2 / 6 | **-94.6R** | **-52.8R** | **yes** |

**M2 is the only candidate that passes every single lane, and its worst cell in
either era is still strongly positive.** Everything else has at least one lane
that is negative in both eras.

**Z is a real second**, but only via arms A, B and C. Arm D is a
trade-*removal* arm (`skip where vol7_prev7 > 1.064`) and it fails IS on both
lanes - which is expected, because it is the removal lever in disguise, and
removals are what just failed 0/4. Read Z as three sizing arms, not four.

**Y and X are dead as universals.** Each wins one lane and loses the others
badly, and X additionally passes on n_oos = 7 and n_oos = 9, which is noise.
Do not promote either.

## The three things that would sink these

1. **Sample size on the forward slice.** The untouched forward data has **5
   trades** against a pre-registered `n >= 50`. Until that clears, no ranking
   here can be called a verdict. This is the binding constraint, and it applies
   to M2 exactly as much as to X and Y.

2. **Z arms A, B and C are one correlated family.** Low edge ratio, wick-heavy
   indecision and contracting volume all mark the same quiet tape; the flagged
   sets overlap heavily. Stacking two of them would 2.25x the same trades.
   **Deploy at most one Z flag, or cap combined exposure.** M2 is a different
   family (entry magnitude) and does not share this problem.

3. **Most of the OOS lift rides a weak baseline.** The OOS baseline is only
   +70.2R over 279 trades. Study 2 (LOG 74) established that OOS deltas on this
   baseline are luck-consistent, so a +30R OOS lift is much weaker evidence than
   the IS number beside it. M2's OOS is the best of the four but it is still
   built on that caveat.

## M2 specifically - the leading candidate

`cur_mag_atr >= 3` -> 1.5x lot. Champion +153.5R IS / +31.5R OOS, and it holds up
on all three lanes including `age10`, which most other candidates do not even
test. The mechanism is the most intuitive of the four: when the current swing
magnitude is already large, the trade sits in a stronger part of the move, so
the same relative risk buys more of a bigger move. It flagged 19-29% of the book
and carried 35-50% of the monsters.

Its one soft spot is that `dNet IS` is roughly 5x `dNet OOS` on every lane, so
most of the measured benefit is in-sample. That is the normal IS/OOS ratio for
this book (baseline is +325.8R IS against +70.2R OOS) and is not disqualifying,
but it does mean the forward test is what decides it.

**M1 (`cur_start <= 1`) must never be adopted**, even though its raw dNet looks
attractive. It flags 71-88% of trades and its "gain" is 1.5x leverage on an
already-positive book, not selection. Per-trade avgR is *worse* on flagged
trades in key cells. CHECKLIST 24.58 calls it a leverage trap and that stands.

## Status

**Nothing here is adopted.** No sizing arm has been forward-tested. The
pre-registered plan is to keep collecting untouched forward data and take no new
filters and no parameter changes until `n >= 50` clears.

Sources: `EXPERIMENT_LOG.md` rows 80-81, `CHECKLIST.md` 24.58 / 24.19,
